meta.preregistration:
# Exp17B decisions fixed before any quantized arm was run (2026-11-25)

Known at this point: BF16 only (identity gate, kernel diagnostics, format probe). No quantization score existed.

1. Determinism: `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`. Without it XPU float matmuls returned up to 16 distinct
   results in 16 identical calls (`exp17b_determinism3.result.log`).
2. Two eval formats, same 2,044 target tokens per domain, run in one process on the same quantized weights:
   - `chat` (PRIMARY): `apply_chat_template([user: "Write out the following document."], add_generation_prompt=True)`
     followed by the 511 content tokens of the window as the model turn. Only the 511 content tokens are scored.
   - `raw` (SECONDARY, the layout in the task text): `<bos>` + the same 511 content tokens.
3. Reason for the primary: on this `-it` checkpoint, raw-text BF16 PPL was about 4e4 (WT2) and 8e2 (Code), outside
   the task's hard sanity bound (not > 100). Chat-wrapped BF16 PPL was inside it in the format probe
   (30.2 / 13.2 with two other prompts, `exp17b_format.result.log`). The prompt above was chosen once and is not tuned.
4. Calibration is wrapped in the same format as the eval it serves. Position 0 is excluded. Content tokens have zero
   6-gram overlap with eval content tokens; the chat template tokens are shared by construction.
5. Gate: `export_biascorr.gate_sidecar`. Primary policy for MLX and HF-INT4-G16 is `BC_all_experts`, and `-b` is the
   exact negation of the same policy. Other policies and W4A8 are exploratory.
6. The verdict quoted for each format is the `chat` verdict. The `raw` verdict is reported next to it, whatever it says.
7. (added after the identity gate passed, still before any quantized arm) Control arm `BF16_rounding_floor_expert_loop`:
   BF16 weights, experts run as a per-expert `F.linear` loop instead of `grouped_mm`. Same math, different rounding.
   Its KL against BF16 is the sensitivity floor of each format. Reason: in the identity gate two such paths differed
   by up to 28 logits on raw text. An arm-to-arm KL difference is not interpreted when it is smaller than that floor.
8. (plumbing correction, from a 6-layer smoke run whose scores are not results) The per-expert BF16 loop in item 7
   turned out bit-identical to `grouped_mm` under deterministic mode, so it perturbs nothing. The control is now
   `BF16_rounding_floor_fp32_expert_matmul`: each expert matmul in FP32, rounded to BF16. Nothing else changed.

arm_definitions.quantized_set: all q/k/v/o_proj, shared mlp gate/up/down_proj and all 128 expert gate_up/down matrices per layer; router, norms, scales and the tied embedding/lm_head stay BF16
arm_definitions.BC: delta_b = (W_bf16 - dequant(W)) @ E[x], FP32, position 0 excluded; for experts E[x] is the unweighted mean over the tokens routed to that expert
arm_definitions.BC_all_experts: dense + every expert with at least 1 routed calibration token (0-token experts get zero)
arm_definitions.BC_threshold_64: dense + experts with at least 64 routed calibration tokens
arm_definitions.tail_blocks: mlp.down_proj K=2112 and experts.down_proj K=704 are 64 mod 128: HF-INT4-G16 arms use Had128 blocks plus one Had64 tail block (NOT supported by the published plugin); SymINT4_G128 uses a 64-wide tail group
arm_definitions.W4A8: FP32 rotation, per-token absmax/127, round-half-even to int8, exact int8xint8 _int_mm, FP32 epilogue; BiasCorr is the weight-error term from BF16-stream means
arm_definitions.Konly_Vonly: attention-only: just k_proj or v_proj is HF-INT4-G16, everything else BF16. On the 5 full layers K=V share k_proj, so Konly also changes V there and Vonly changes nothing; Konly_slidingLayersOnly is the matched comparison
arm_definitions.pluginLoadableScope: HF-INT4-G16 on dense linears with K%128==0 only; mlp.down_proj and all experts BF16

reading_of_results_chat_primary: All four primary gates PUBLISHABLE; every primary +b improvement exceeds the chat rounding floor.
Data-free combined KL: HF-INT4-G16 0.158 and NVFP4 0.169 are not separable (paired delta -0.011, CI -0.025 to +0.003); HF-INT4-G16 beats MLX G64 (0.262) and Sym G128 (0.449).

MoE BiasCorr: all_experts and threshold_64 are not separable from attention+shared-MLP-only for MLX or HF-INT4-G16 (combined CIs span 0, deltas below the 0.0084 combined floor). Measured gain comes from the dense linears. Calibration was 2,044 positions per format (median 88 routed tokens per expert slot, 212 of 3,840 slots with none), so this does not show per-expert correction cannot help with more calibration data.
W4A8 vs W4A16 (HF-INT4-G16, data-free): combined delta +0.0028, CI -0.0016 to +0.0071.
V-sensitive: V-only KL exceeds K-only, including the matched sliding-layers-only comparison (0.050 vs 0.019 combined).
claim_boundary: Harness evidence only: weights are dequantized in memory (W4A8 uses a live int8 path). No vLLM engine run, no serving speed, no shipped quantized checkpoint.
chat PPL is 24.6 (WT2) and 11.9 (Code): inside the 3-100 hard bound, WT2 outside the expected 5-9. The chat wrapper is a deviation from the raw-token layout in the task.

Raw-text BF16 PPL 40294 / 772. Reproduced by HF modeling code on CPU FP32 eager at 128 tokens (before determinism was enabled on XPU; CPU path is independent of XPU kernels). That it is a property of the -it checkpoint is an inference; no third-party engine was run.
Raw format rounding floor is 0.40 / 0.64 KL; use gate_vs_rounding_floor before quoting any raw verdict.
Determinism makes repeat runs bit-identical. It does not make results independent of kernel or batch shape; the rounding-floor arm measures that sensitivity with one perturbation only.
95% intervals resample 32-position blocks inside 4 windows per domain. They do not cover choice of documents, calibration set or prompt.
Had128NoPerm arms use a Had64 tail block for K=2112 and K=704; the published plugin cannot do this.
MLX, NVFP4 and Sym arms are this harness's reimplementations of those formats, not third-party checkpoints.
